why: Every value is derived by hand from voxelize.wgsl's widened-edge rule: a cell is covered when its centre lies within 0.5 of the triangle's inside-positive edges, the dominant-axis scan runs over floor(min)..floor(max) of the projected box, and z spans floor(depth +/- spread). No value comes from a GPU run or from the code under test.

quad.why: R=8, normal +z, two triangles on w=2.25 spanning u [1,3] and v [1,2]. The x scan stays at floor(min)=1..floor(max)=3 and the y scan at floor(1)=1..floor(2)=2, because the widened span cannot undo the projected box's floor; every centre is within 0.5 of the outer edges, so the 3x2 cells are covered. depth 2.25 with spread 0 gives the single z cell floor(2.25)=2. Sorted by (x,y,z).

sliver.why: Thin triangle (1,4,3),(7,4,3),(7,4.2,3) along x. The y scan is the single row floor(4)=4..floor(4.2)=4; its centre 4.5 is within 0.5 of both long edges, so the row is covered. The x span is [1.5,7.5], giving cells 1..7 with no gap. Constant depth 3 gives z=3.

outside.why: x starts at 10, more than one voxel beyond R=8 (the skip limit is 8+1=9), so the projected box_min[0] check returns before any cell is emitted.

clip_span.why: slope 0 with offset 2 >= 0 keeps the whole span
slope 0 with offset -0.25 < 0 empties the span to (1, 0)
